newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds Metals reorganizes global operation.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds Metals reorganizes global operation.

text.p: Reynolds Metals Co said Thursday it was reorganizing into six worldwide, market-focused businesses, effective April 1.

The organizational and management changes are intended to focus the company on global aluminum markets that are most promising for profitable growth, said Jeremiah Sheehan, Reynolds chairman and chief executive.
In January the company reported a loss of $0.13 a share for the 1996 fourth quarter, while three of its rivals posted profits.
Sheehan said Reynolds had been organized into 20 operating units, including a primarily U.S.-focused group and a separate international group.
He said a spin-off of the packaging business was still under review.
"If and when we decide to proceed with that option, our new organization structure will better position that business for becoming an independent company," he said.
Under the reorganization, Randolph Reynolds, 55, vice chairman and executive officer, will be responsible for four new global units.
J. Wilt Wagner, 55, also vice chairman and executive officer, will lead implementation of the company's review of its portfolio, which will primarily involve managing divestitures.
Reynolds and Wagner will both report to Sheehan.
The four new units and their heads are construction and distribution, Donald Cowles; transportation, Eugene Desvernine; metals and carbon products, Paul Ratki, and bauxite and alumina, Larry Hawkins.
Also reporting to Sheehan will be Thomas Christino, head of the global packaging and consumer products business, and William Leahey Jr, head of the global can business.
The company said the office of chief executive will continue to consist of Sheehan, Reynolds, Wagner and Henry Savedge Jr, executive vice president and chief financial officer.
